title: Real-time dynamics of triplet-resonant tunneling driven by nonequilibrium phonons
authors: Kazuyuki Kuroyama, Sasha R. Valentin, Arne Ludwig, Andreas D. Wieck, Yasuhiro Tokura, Seigo Tarucha, Sadashige Matsuo
abstract: Driven nonequilibrium systems can host emergent functionalities beyond equilibrium, but real-time access to excited-state dynamics remains limited. Here we report real-time measurements of phonon-driven charge and spin dynamics in excited states of a double quantum dot. Under phonon irradiation, resonant inter-dot tunneling emerges at triplet resonance. Time-resolved charge sensing reveals that the resonant inter-dot tunneling is strongly modified by spin blockade. For weaker inter-dot coupling, the nonequilibrium phonon environment generates a unidirectional transport cycle along the phonon density gradient.
summary: The researchers measured the real-time charge and spin dynamics in a double quantum dot driven by nonequilibrium phonons. They found that at triplet resonance, the phonon environment induces strong rectification, leading to a measurable current via unidirectional electron transport cycles. This demonstrates how non-equilibrium driving can generate directed quantum currents in solid-state devices.
main_problem: The study investigates real-time charge and spin dynamics in excited states of a double quantum dot (DQD) driven by nonequilibrium phonons to understand emergent functionalities beyond equilibrium.
main_result: The system exhibits strong, measurable rectification ($\eta \approx 1$) leading to unidirectional electron transport cycles when driven by the phonon gradient at triplet resonance conditions.
method: Time-resolved charge sensing and rate analysis are used to track inter-dot tunneling events under controlled nonequilibrium phonon irradiation.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a semiconductor DQD fabricated on an AlGaAs/GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure, coupled with a nearby phonon source QD. Dynamics are analyzed using spin states (Singlet/Triplet) and rate equations derived from time-resolved measurements.
key_observables: Inter-dot resonant tunneling rates ($\Gamma$), waiting-time histograms, current ($I \sim 10^{-19}$ A), and rectification parameter ($\eta$).
important_parameters: Low temperature ($\approx 20$ mK); detuning voltage ($V_R$); phonon bias voltage ($V_{PS}$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are governed by the coupling between electronic states and the nonequilibrium phonon bath, allowing for rate-equation descriptions.
figures_summary: Figures show charge stability diagrams revealing new triplet resonances (Fig. 1c); time traces illustrate resonant tunneling at both singlet and triplet conditions (Fig. 2a/b); waiting-time histograms compare rates across resonance types (Fig. 3); and later figures detail the unidirectional current generation and rectification ($\eta$) in weak coupling regimes (Fig. 4).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the experimental setup and observing basic resonant tunneling at singlet/triplet resonances, to quantifying dwell times using waiting-time statistics, and finally demonstrating nonreciprocal transport by analyzing current generation and rectification ($\eta$) in the weak coupling limit.
why_interesting: This work provides a direct experimental realization of non-equilibrium quantum dynamics, showing how external energy baths (phonons) can induce directed, non-reciprocal transport cycles in mesoscopic solid-state systems, which is highly relevant to open quantum system physics and energy harvesting concepts.
